title: token-stitcher: stitch tokenizer fragments between regex & grammar constraints to preserve tool-call framing
author: Aisha Kaur
description:
Motivation: We observed recurring corruption of tool/function call framing and structured outputs when combining multiple constrained-decoding backends (CFG/grammar + regex). The root cause is partial tokenizer fragment emission at stream boundaries: regex backends sometimes emit matches that split in the middle of bytepair subtokens, and the grammar backend expects atomic symbol boundaries. This manifests as truncated JSON tool-call payloads, missing closing delimiters in streaming responses, and brittle OpenAI-compat framing behavior.

Summary: This PR implements a lightweight `token-stitcher` layer inside the constraint muxer that sits between the tokenizer shim and individual constraint backends. The stitcher tracks partial subtoken runs, attributes them to a constraint "origin" (regex|grammar|fallback), and applies deterministic heuristics to decide whether to delay emission, merge fragments, or re-tokenize a small window to restore atomic boundaries. Key heuristics: 1) anchor-precedence — prefer grammar anchors if they encompass the same byte range as a regex match; 2) subtoken-lookahead — when a backend produces a fragment that does not end on a stable boundary, hold up to 4 subtokens to see if the following backend will complete the token (configurable window); 3) fallback-trim — if a fragment is still incomplete after the hold window, rewrite boundary by emitting a safe escape separator ("\uFFF0") and annotate the stream event so OpenAI-compat adapters can recover.

Compatibility & API: The streaming protocol is unchanged. To support OpenAI compatibility we add an internal stream annotation header `x-rw-token-stitch` that the `openai_stream_adapter` will map to chunked JSON events used by the SDKs. The feature is behind a runtime feature-flag `token_stitcher.enabled` (default: true) and a tuning option `token_stitcher.lookahead` (default: 4).

Files changed (high level): core/decoder/constraint_muxer.py - new TokenStitcher class and orchestration logic; core/decoder/tokenizer_shim.py - minor API to expose partial-subtoken markers; api/compat/openai_stream_adapter.py - map stitch annotations to OpenAI-compatible framing; tests/test_constraint_streaming.py - extensive unit + integration coverage including bilingual BytePair boundary cases and tool-call JSON streaming; docs/structured-output.md - design notes and rollback instructions.

Testing & CI: Added deterministic fuzz tests that simulate split-token regex matches and grammar anchor collisions across multiple languages (English, Japanese). CI shows one flaky test initially (test_stream_reassembly) which was fixed by tightening the lookahead window for Japanese multi-byte sequences. End-to-end synthetic load tests on a local 4xA100 cluster show ~0.6% median token-latency increase for unconstrained workloads when the stitcher is enabled, while structured-output workloads with mixed constraints regained 98-100% of previously lost tool-call frames (previously ~12% corruption).

Risk & rollback: The change touches streaming hot paths. Risks: small latency regression and complexity in the muxer. Rollback is a single feature-flag flip (token_stitcher.enabled=false) and a hotfix revert (two-file revert) if necessary. We validated fallbacks with Dedicated and Private deployments.

Release notes: Improve stability of streaming structured output when combining CFG/grammar and regex constraints; introduces `token_stitcher` to reduce token-boundary corruption for tool/function calling and OpenAI-compatible streaming; configurable via runtime feature flags.

Related: ENG-4921 (root investigation), SUP-884 (customer report for tool-call truncation).

review_comments: Connor Liu: The heuristics look reasonable but we should avoid holding tokens for long under high-qps. Can we gate lookahead by request size? -- Author reply: added a per-request budget cap (max_hold_subtokens) and tests to ensure backpressure behaves well.

Priya Desai: Please add explicit instrumentation (metric) for stitcher holds and escapes so SRE can alert on regressions. -- Author reply: instrumented rw.stitcher.holds and rw.stitcher.escaped_fragments; added dashboards in observability backlog.

Miguel Rivera: Concern about OpenAI compatibility header leaking into public SDKs. Suggest mapping to existing chunk meta instead. -- Author reply: changed to map to existing openai chunk 'meta' envelope; header remains internal to platform.
Connor Liu: Minor nit on naming: token_stitcher vs stitcher. -- Author reply: standardized on TokenStitcher class and token_stitcher.* config keys.
Priya Desai: Approve after doc clarifies rollback steps. -- Author reply: docs updated with step-by-step rollback and feature-flag toggle examples.
ci_summary: All checks passed on main: unit (pass), integration (pass), fuzz (pass), lint (pass), e2e (pass). One flaky test fixed during iteration.
release_notes: Stabilizes streaming structured output with mixed constraint backends by adding TokenStitcher heuristics; configurable lookahead and opt-out flag. Recommended for any customers with tool/function calling across constrained prompts.
notes_for_release: Enable by default; monitor rw.stitcher.holds and rw.stitcher.escaped_fragments. Rollback: set token_stitcher.enabled=false and cut a quick patch release if needed.
ci_reruns: One rerun for flaky fuzz test (test_stream_reassembly) resolved; no further reruns required.
backport_instructions: Backport to release/2026-02 for Dedicated and Private deploys: cherry-pick TokenStitcher class and tokenizer_shim API only; keep openai_stream_adapter change gated behind feature-flag until SDKs are aligned.
manual_migration_steps: None required for customers; internal ops: rotate feature-flag per-region when enabling rollout to avoid global impact.
changelog_entry: Added TokenStitcher to improve streaming stability for constrained decoding (CFG + regex) and prevent tool-call truncation.
audit_notes: Logged stitcher decisions with correlation ids for 30 days; added a short-lived debug mode to capture raw subtoken traces for customer-reported cases.
